risks.risk: The drivetrain (chain, cassette, and chainrings) may be excessively worn.
risks.proof: A clear, close-up photo of the teeth on the rear cassette and front chainrings.
risks.if_unproven: as needing a full drivetrain replacement

risks.risk: The disc brakes may be non-functional or have worn-out pads.
risks.proof: A video showing the wheels spinning freely and then being stopped abruptly by the brakes.

risks.risk: The front suspension fork may be seized or leaking oil.
risks.proof: A video of a rider leaning on the handlebars to show the fork compressing and rebounding smoothly.

risks.risk: The gears may not shift correctly due to a bent derailleur or stretched cables.
risks.proof: A video of the bike being pedaled while shifting through all available gear combinations.
risks.if_unproven: as stuck in a single gear

risks.risk: The seatpost may be seized inside the frame.
risks.proof: A photo showing the seatpost adjusted to a different height.
risks.if_unproven: as fixed at the current height

proof_requests: A clear photo of the model number (e.g., ST120, 520) usually found on the top tube or near the seat post.
Close-up photos of the gear teeth and the brake calipers.
A video demonstrating the gear shifting and the suspension movement.
A photo of the underside of the frame to check for cracks or heavy impact damage.
